hints: A necessary road is a bridge: removing it disconnects the graph.
A DFS subtree can escape without its parent edge only through a back edge to an ancestor.
Track discovery time and the earliest ancestor reachable from each subtree.
analogy: A bridge is a branch with no alternate rope connecting its far side back to the trunk.
example: In a triangle with an extra edge from one vertex to a leaf, only the leaf edge is necessary.
algorithm: Run depth-first search, recording discovery times and low values. The low value of a vertex is the smallest discovery time reachable from its subtree using tree edges and at most one back edge. A DFS tree edge from v to child u is a bridge exactly when low[u] > discovery[v]. Output all such edges.
correctness: If low[u] exceeds discovery[v], the subtree has no alternate edge to v or an ancestor, so removing the tree edge disconnects it. Otherwise an alternate path bypasses the edge. Non-tree edges lie on cycles and cannot be bridges.
complexity: For n cities and m roads, O(n+m) time and O(n+m) space.
